description:
## Background

Renderer tests prove Graph projection and interaction deterministically, but they do not prove that real Beadwork relationship data crosses the Rust/TauRPC boundary into the built desktop application and participates in browser history correctly. The first Graph release needs one narrow slice-level desktop proof, matching the repository's existing WebDriver strategy.

The required path is intentionally small: Graph → Issue Detail → Close → Back. Exhaustive lifecycle and visual regression coverage belong in renderer tests, not in a slow desktop matrix.

Triage: ready-for-agent.

## What to build

Add one real-desktop WebDriver scenario that launches the built Tauri binary with a disposable Beadwork Workspace and proves the completed Graph navigation path against authored parent and blocker relationships.

## Technical Approach

- Extend the existing Issue List WebDriver harness rather than creating a new driver stack or mock renderer.
- Create a scenario-owned disposable Workspace through real `bw` commands.
- Author a compact fixture containing Current Work, a closed direct parent, a direct blocker, a blocked Issue, and an unrelated closed Issue that appears only in Show all.
- Select the Workspace through the existing typed TauRPC boundary and wait for the successful Issue Explorer snapshot.
- Enter Graph through the sidebar and assert Focused scope includes the Current Work plus its direct parent and blocker while omitting the unrelated closed Issue.
- Assert parent and blocker relationships expose distinct DOM/test semantics and the correct directions without relying on pixel coordinates.
- Switch to Show all and prove the unrelated closed Issue appears.
- Activate an Issue card, assert the existing Issue Detail content in the Graph overlay, Close it, and use Back to reopen it.
- Keep selectors in shared helpers where they encode Graph semantics.
- Document the new scenario and its command in `docs/agents/webdriver-e2e.md`.

## Considerations

- Use the real built desktop binary, real Beadwork CLI data, typed TauRPC Workspace selection, and the existing isolated store.
- Do not mock React Flow, the Issue transport, or browser history in this scenario.
- Do not assert exact card coordinates, SVG paths, colors, frame timing, or screenshots.
- Renderer suites remain responsible for viewport preservation, refresh permutations, Workspace switch failures, missing endpoints, keyboard matrices, and representative-size performance.
- Reuse the existing embedded WebDriver port and scenario process lifecycle unless a documented harness constraint requires otherwise.
- Scenario-owned repositories and stores must be cleaned up and must never touch the developer's normal Workspace catalog.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A documented desktop scenario launches the real Beadsmith debug binary with an isolated Graph fixture.
- [ ] The fixture is created with real Beadwork commands and carries explicit parent and blocker relationships through TauRPC.
- [ ] Focused Graph shows Current Work, its closed direct parent, and direct blocker while omitting an unrelated closed Issue.
- [ ] Parent and blocker relationships have distinct, correctly directed test semantics.
- [ ] Show all reveals the unrelated closed Issue.
- [ ] Card activation opens the reused Issue Detail overlay.
- [ ] Close removes the overlay by pushing an unselected Graph entry, and Back reopens it.
- [ ] The scenario leaves the developer's normal catalog untouched and removes its temporary resources.
- [ ] Existing desktop scenarios remain green.
- [ ] `mise run doctor:react` and `mise run verify` pass.

## Test Plan

- Run the new Graph WebDriver scenario through its documented harness command.
- Run the existing Issue List success scenario to catch shared-harness and sidebar regressions.
- Run the canonical `mise run verify` gate.
- Record any upstream WebDriver caveat in the existing E2E documentation rather than weakening assertions with arbitrary sleeps.
title: Prove Graph Mode in the real desktop application
